content.text:
The fix is on a new branch, `fix/persist-compose-drafts`. Drafts no longer get lost: pressing back, switching away from the app, swiping it out of recents, or a crash all keep what you wrote, including images and files. Tests, typecheck and Biome all pass. Nothing is committed or pushed, and I haven't run it on a device or emulator yet.

## Why drafts were lost
- **Text, tags, date and location** were only kept in the screen's memory. Leaving the screen threw them away, and so did the app being closed.
- **Photos, recordings and files** were only references to the phone's temporary cache. They were copied somewhere permanent only when you pressed save, and Android can clear that cache once the app is gone.
- There was no autosave, nothing ran when the app went to the background, and nothing loaded a draft back.

## How it works now
1. **Saved to disk, not the database.** Each draft has its own folder under `drafts/`: one for a new entry, and one per entry being edited. Keeping it out of the database means it never ends up in backups. Text is written to a temporary file first and then swapped in, so a crash halfway through a write keeps the previous version.
2. **Picked files get their own copy.** Each photo, recording or file is copied once, so clearing the cache can't break the draft. Copies you remove from the draft are deleted.
3. **When it saves:** half a second after you stop changing things, straight away when the app leaves the foreground (swiping it away from recents always does this first), and when you leave the screen.
4. **When it restores:** opening a new entry brings back the unsaved one. Opening an entry you were editing goes straight back into edit mode with your changes.
5. **When it clears:** only after the entry is safely saved to the database. It also clears if you empty the draft, press Cancel on an edit, delete that entry, or use "Delete all entries".
6. **Defensive restore.** A damaged draft file is ignored, file paths are checked, lists have a size limit, and any file that has since disappeared is dropped.

## Changed files
- New: [snapshot.ts](src/services/drafts/snapshot.ts) (draft format and checks) and [store.ts](src/services/drafts/store.ts) (reading and writing drafts on disk).
- Autosave and restore: [useComposeDraft.ts](src/modules/compose/hooks/useComposeDraft.ts), [useMediaAttachments.ts](src/modules/compose/hooks/useMediaAttachments.ts), [Compose.tsx](src/screens/compose/Compose.tsx). `useLocation.reset` can now reset to a given location.
- Cleanup on delete: [EntryStore.ts](src/modules/entry/store/EntryStore.ts).
- New tests: [test-draft-snapshot.mjs](scripts/test-draft-snapshot.mjs).

## Limits and things to know
- A voice recording still in progress when the app dies is not saved. Finished recordings are.
- A restored draft keeps its own date and tags. Opening a new entry from a tag's timeline won't add that tag to an older draft.
- Big files take up space twice while they're in a draft, until you save or discard it.
- Importing a backup doesn't remove drafts for entries that the import replaced. They just sit unused on disk.
- There is no "Discard draft" button for new entries. You clear one by deleting its content. A discard button would be a small follow-up if you want one.
- **Still needs a device check:** swipe away from recents, a forced crash, Android clearing its cache, and restoring on an iOS reinstall or update.

I fixed the real problems the two reviewers found. Tests (31), typecheck and Biome all pass. Nothing is committed or pushed, and none of it has been run on a device or emulator yet.

**Problems that could still cost you a draft, now fixed:**
- **A failed save was never retried.** If a write failed, the same content was never written again. Now it retries on the next change or the next time you leave.
- **One missing file lost the whole draft.** If a photo was already cleared from the cache, the text was lost too. Now only that one item is dropped.
- **Leaving quickly could lose the last keystrokes.** If you pressed back and reopened a new entry while the screen was still animating out, the new screen could load the older autosave. Now it saves when back is pressed, before the animation starts.
- **A crash during a write could restore the older version.** Now the newer copy is read first if it's complete.

**Smaller glitches, now fixed:**
- A leftover draft that was empty, or identical to the entry, could force the entry into edit mode every time and never get cleared. It's now ignored and cleaned up on the next autosave.
- All drafts shared one queue, so copying a large file for one draft made every other entry wait to open. Each draft now has its own queue; "Delete all" still waits for all of them.
- After saving a new entry, its draft files were deleted while the closing screen could still be showing their previews. They're now cleared after you're taken back.
- Importing a backup now clears drafts, so an old edit can't overwrite the imported entry.

**Code cleanup:**
- Draft files reuse the existing media filename and extension helpers instead of a copy of them.
- The "is this draft worth keeping" rule now lives in one function in `DraftTransform.ts`, shared by the autosave and the screen.
- `reset` always takes an explicit target, and a stale comment is gone.
- I didn't add any test files; the one from before covers the draft format and path checks.

**Known limits, left as they are:**
- **A recording still in progress** when you leave or the app dies is not saved. Finished recordings are. Fixing that means stopping the recorder when you leave, which changes how recording behaves.
- **Typing during the moment an edit is saving** is replaced by the saved version. Keeping it would have meant a hidden draft behind the view screen.
- **Backup files with spaces or unusual characters in their names** get copied into the draft while you edit. The result is still correct; it just copies more than it needs to. Files the app creates don't hit this.
- **Leaving the app during a very large file copy:** the text is written only after the copy finishes, so it can be lost if the app dies mid-copy. The half-second autosave has usually copied the file already.

| 7 | Pressed Cancel on that edit, killed the app, reopened | ✅ Saved version shown; edit draft cleared |

**What I couldn't fully cover:**
- **Clearing the app's cache** (what Android does when space runs low) hung on your phone, so I stopped it. Its data was fine afterwards, but I can't confirm the cache was actually cleared, so that case is only partly tested.

- Attached files come back with the draft.

Text typed during the brief moment an edit is saving is replaced by the saved version. okay whats the delay?

It isn't a fixed delay. The window lasts from tapping save until the entry is written. For an edit with no new media that's a few milliseconds, too short for anyone to type into. In test 8 on your phone it looked instant.

It only gets longer when the edit adds new files, because saving copies each new file into permanent storage first:

| Edit | Rough save time |
|---|---|
| Text, tags, date or location only | A few milliseconds |
| New photos (about 0.5–2 MB each) | Tens of milliseconds |
| A big new attachment, like a 100 MB+ video | Up to a second or more |

Files that were already on the entry aren't copied again, so they add nothing.

This window has nothing to do with the 500 ms autosave delay; that only decides when a draft gets written to disk.

Yes, I'd release it on Android. iOS is the one thing I'd check first.

**Why it's safe:**
- **No database change.** Drafts live in a separate `drafts/` folder, so there's no migration, and existing entries, media and backups aren't touched.
- **The risk is small and recoverable.** If draft code fails, it reports the error and the app keeps working the way it did before. Saving entries goes through the same path as before; the draft is only cleared after the entry is committed.
- **It's been checked end to end:** unit tests, typecheck and Biome, two independent reviews, and 11 passing tests on your phone. Those covered back, background, swipe-kill, force-stop, a cache wipe, files, gallery photos, recordings, editing, cancelling and saving.

**Before you release:**
1. **iOS:** if you ship iOS too, try it once on a simulator or iPhone. The code is the same, but iOS backgrounding and file paths haven't been run.
2. **Do the usual release change** from AGENTS.md: bump `expo.version` and `package.json` together, add 1 to `ios.buildNumber` and `android.versionCode`, add a changelog section, and run `pnpm expo:doctor`. For "What's new", something like: *"Unsaved writing, photos, files and recordings are now kept as a draft if you leave or the app closes."*
3. **Delete the local `android/` folder** (`rm -rf android`). It's git-ignored, so neither EAS nor the Play release workflow will use it. But it's my test setup: a separate app ID, a debuggable build, and Gradle pointed at a temporary file. A local Android build would pick it up by mistake.

**Known gaps to ship with:** a recording still in progress when the app closes is lost, and there's the few-millisecond window where text typed during an edit-save gets replaced. Neither is a regression; both lost data before this change as well.
